gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: The promenade has ramped, step free access and wide routes along the seafront. The sand is hard going with wheels, and it gets congested at busy times, so I would pick your pitch on the prom early.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Dogs are allowed on a lead, but the show strongly advises against bringing them because of the noise, and off lead dogs mean you’re asked to leave. I would think about how yours copes with jets before you decide.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: You can bring your own food, but BBQs, gas and open fires aren’t allowed. Alcohol isn’t mentioned, and the Sefton coast has an order letting officers tell you to stop drinking, so I would leave it at home.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Your own chairs are welcome as long as they don’t block paths, accessible areas or anyone’s view. Gazebos and windbreaks aren’t mentioned, so I would ask the show before you pack one.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: I haven’t found any refill points listed for the show. I would bring plenty of water, as there’s very little shade on the seawall.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There isn’t one on the site, but you’re given a pass out stamp so you can use one and come back. In 2026 the closest weekend options were Victoria Park on the Esplanade, 10:00 to 18:00, and Dunes Splashworld, 09:00 to 16:00.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: In 2026 a carer got in free with proof such as Carer’s Allowance, Attendance Allowance, DLA or PIP, with the ticket issued at the box office. Without the paperwork the carer pays on the gate, so please bring it with you.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I haven’t found anything on hearing loops or BSL. I would email Tourism@sefton.gov.uk before you go, as they handle accessibility questions for the show.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There’s no calm or sensory space listed. The show itself suggests arriving when the gates open for a quieter time, and I would bring ear defenders or noise cancelling headphones.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: It’s a gated, ticketed site. A pass out stamp was confirmed in 2026 for visiting a Changing Places toilet, but for anything else I would ask at the gate before you leave.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: The show hasn’t said where first aid or a lost children point will be, but stewards are spread right along the site. I would agree a meeting point when you arrive and write your phone number on younger children’s wrists.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm, and remember the wind comes straight off the Irish Sea here.

days.html:
Pick Your Day

Southport runs over the Saturday and Sunday of the August bank holiday weekend. In 2026 the two days were very alike, with the Red Arrows on both. The big difference was the RAF Typhoon, which only flew on the Sunday. When I last checked, the 2027 dates and line-up hadn’t been announced.

Dates2027 to be confirmed
Gates10:00 (2026)
FlyingAbout 12:00 to 17:00
TyphoonSunday in 2026
SaturdayIn 2026 the gates opened at 10:00 and the flying ran from about 12:00 to 17:00, with the Red Arrows, the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight and the full civilian line-up. No Typhoon.
SundayThe same times in 2026, with the Red Arrows again and the RAF Typhoon closing the show. Merseyrail runs every 30 minutes from Liverpool on a Sunday, rather than every 15.

Is the Typhoon a must?

Who’s coming?

How are you travelling?

I Would Pick The Saturday

  1. WhyYou still get the Red Arrows and the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, without the Typhoon, which is the loudest jet of the weekend. This might work for your family if anyone is sensitive to noise.
  2. Good to knowWhatever day you pick, your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible. I would still pack ear defenders.
  3. Getting thereMerseyrail runs every 15 minutes from Liverpool on a Saturday. The station is about ten minutes’ walk from the seafront.

I Would Pick The Sunday

  1. WhyIn 2026 the RAF Typhoon closed the show on the Sunday only. If you’re into fast jets, that’s the one I would go for.
  2. Good to knowIn 2026 the Monday was the bank holiday, so there was no rush to get home for work. Heavy rain cut the Red Arrows short that Sunday, which is just the luck of the weather.
  3. Getting thereMerseyrail drops to every 30 minutes on a Sunday, so I would plan your train home before you settle in. There’s more in .
Jack’s tipThe line-up for each day is only confirmed nearer the show. I would wait for the 2027 list before booking anything, as there’s no promise the Typhoon will be on the Sunday again.

Based on the 2026 show. The 2027 dates, line-up and times may change.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

The gates open about two hours before the flying, so there’s plenty of time to look round. Most of it sits along Marine Drive. There are no real aircraft on static display, only replicas, but the Military Village and the rides keep most families busy until midday.

WhereMarine Drive
Gates10:00 (2026)
CostIncluded in entry
RidesPay as you go
In 2026

The Military Village

Armed Forces equipment displays on Marine Drive, with the Royal Navy, British Army and RAF there to chat to, and the local Air Cadets too. I’ve said more about it in the .

In 2026

Replica Chinook

A replica Chinook sat in the Military Village. It’s a great photo for the kids, and you get a feel for just how big it is.

In 2026

Typhoon Display Team Stand

The RAF Typhoon Display Team had their own stand. I would visit before the flying, as it’s a nice way to learn about the jet you’ll see later.

In 2026

Military Vehicles And Living History

Restored vehicles from the Mid Lancs Military Vehicle Trust, Second World War displays from the Garrison Artillery Volunteers and the Veterans Living History Museum.

In 2026

Flight Simulators

Hands on cockpit simulators near the Military Village. Children love to have a go, and it’s a good one for teenagers too.

Pay as you go

Rides And Games

Bungee trampolines, bumper cars, Hook a Duck, face glitter and hair braiding in 2026. There’s more for little ones in .

Pay as you go

Marine Drive Stalls

Market stalls with aviation artwork, military memorabilia, collectables, toys and sweets, alongside the food and drink traders. Food and toilets are covered in .

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the seawall or the beach as soon as the gates open and set up your chairs or blanket.
  2. Then walk Marine DriveTake a look round the Military Village, speak to the crews, visit the trade stalls and check the food options while it’s still quiet.
  3. Toilet before the flyingI would go before midday, as the queues build quickly once the first aircraft appear.
  4. Use the gapsIf you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use it as a toilet or food break.
Jack’s tipThe site gets very busy from late morning. I would do the Military Village and the simulators first, in that first hour after the gates open, and leave the stalls for a gap in the flying.

Exhibitors and attractions change each year, so the 2027 ground show may look different.

skipped.flights: No pleasure, helicopter, warbird or balloon flights are offered at or from the show. The only flying experience on site is the ground based flight simulators, which are in the ground show.
skipped.support: Southport is a ticketed show (in 2026, £13 adult plus booking fee, under 16s free), and I found no donation, bucket collection or volunteer appeal, so a Keep the show free section doesn't suit it.

notes: 1) 2027 dates still not announced as of 3 Nov 2026; Sefton has only said Southport hosts national Armed Forces Day in 2027 (https://sefton.gov.uk/mysefton-news/latest-news/the-sky-was-the-limit-as-southport-air-show-returns-in-style/). 2) Food and facilities, Accessibility: the page lists Changing Places at Victoria Park, Dunes Splashworld, Southport Market, The Life Rooms and The Atkinson. In the 2026 accessibility guide The Life Rooms is open Monday to Friday only and The Atkinson is closed on Sundays, so for a weekend show only Victoria Park (10:00 to 18:00), Dunes Splashworld (09:00 to 16:00 at weekends) and Southport Market (Sat 10:00 to 23:00, Sun 10:00 to 18:30) are really useful (https://assets.simpleviewinc.com/simpleview/image/upload/v1/clients/southport/Accessibility_Guide_Southport_Airshow_2026_73c84977-35ed-4873-a48b-4f07d826cb53.pdf). 3) Carers: the page lists Carer's Allowance, Attendance Allowance or DLA; the official air show page also accepts PIP (https://www.visitsouthport.com/airshow). 4) The 2026 accessibility guide's feature list says 'Static aircraft and military exhibits', but the main show page only mentions replica aircraft; I kept the page's 'replicas only' line, so I left out the 'aircraft opened up and merch' line. 5) The accessibility guide suggests arriving when the gates open for a quieter visit, and says portable seating is welcome if it doesn't block routes or views; neither is on the page yet. 6) Dune Radio 'Southport Air Show LIVE' is on DAB+, online, smart speakers and the RadioPlayer app; the page only mentions travel updates.
